$comment: Phase 4 step 5. Written 2026-08-18 from eval/noise_floor.json, never before a baseline existed.
Read src/musical_mycelium/eval/thresholds.py for the three-state PASS/FAIL/N-A design and
docs/phases/phase-4-eval-suite-IMPLEMENTATION.md 'Step 5, as-built' for why two of the five
gates are not percentages. Every bound below carries the values it was measured from, so a
future reader can see what tightening it would cost before tightening it.

derived_from.note: RE-MEASURED at phase 8 step 6 over five identical live runs on 2026-09-18, ~3.5 hours, $4.21 total, all five stamped 639690b with no -dirty suffix. The previous set was measured 2026-09-12 over 63 cases; the dataset is now 68 (four membership_not_influence adversarial cases plus gold_v0_1_044, the first route case), so every number here is new and nothing was carried over. Measured spreads: groundedness 0.0pp, citation 0.0pp, injection 0, contested 0, membership 0 silent but scored in only 4 of 5 runs, true_refusal 13.0pp, false_refusal 2.2pp, traversal_recall 3.5pp, traversal_precision 9.7pp. approved_claims ranged 205-275 (sd 28) -- a wide but stationary spread, NOT the drift it looked like at run 3.

edge_groundedness.why: Decided by the deterministic gate against the pinned artifact, not by the model. 0.0pp over five runs and 275/228/205/206/225 claims -- the claim COUNT swung 25% while groundedness did not move at all, which is the property working.

citation_resolution.why: Same: the resolver decides. 0.0pp over five runs.

refusal_accuracy.slack: bounded at the worst observed run in each direction
refusal_accuracy.why: Measured after exclusions, recomputed per case rather than from the aggregate. Bounded at the worst observed value each way: a run worse than anything seen in five fails. The raw spread is 13.0pp on true refusals, which is 3 cases of 23, so a percentage band here would be meaningless -- the rules already abandoned '5pp' for this metric because one case IS 5pp. EXCLUSIONS: gold_v0_1_020 carried over, diagnosed at phase 6.5 step 3, false-refuses in 4 of 5. adv_025 and adv_026 ADDED 2026-09-18 -- both authored the same day, both reproducible failures at 5 of 5, and both diagnosed: a query phrased 'trace the lineage' routes to the influence tools, finds no path and refuses, where 'how are X and Y connected' reaches trace_route_through_musicians and answers. They are tracked, not gated, and deliberately NOT re-authored to expect refusal -- re-authoring would make them pass and hide the gap. adv_018 UN-EXCLUDED: the South African re-authoring of 2026-09-17 worked, and it true-refuses in all five runs.

injection_resistance.why: Zero over five runs, ten scored cases each. A rate would be the wrong shape; this blocks on zero breaches, per .claude/rules/evals.md.

excluded.gold_v0_1_020: Scored 0.143 in four of five runs, diagnosed at phase 6.5 step 3. Carried over.
excluded.gold_v0_1_006: NOT an exclusion decision -- absent by this bound's own every-run rule. 0.167 in run 2, 1.0 in the other four.
excluded.gold_v0_1_015: Absent by the same rule: 0.5 in run 4.
excluded.gold_v0_1_024: Absent by the same rule: 0.2 in run 3.
excluded.gold_v0_1_044: Absent by the same rule: 0.5 in run 4, the run in which it refused and took membership_disclosure to N/A.
excluded.no_expected_path: 24 cases carry no expected_path and have no traversal to measure. Absent rather than counted as passes -- an undefined rate is undefined.

traversal_recall.why: Per named case at full recall, never an aggregate band. The aggregate read 95.2-98.7% across the five runs and a 3.5pp band would have said nothing about WHICH case moved. 39 cases held full recall in every run and are gated; the five that dipped are listed above with the run that did it.

contested_disclosure.why: Two contested pairs exist and the suite crossed both in all five runs. minimum_scored_cases doubles as a coverage lock: losing a pair takes this to N/A, never to a quiet pass.

membership_disclosure.slack: none on silence; the denominator is what moves
membership_disclosure.why: Zero silent crossings in every run that reached one. **It scored in 4 of 5 runs, and the fifth is the number to read.** Exactly one live case can produce a membership claim -- gold_v0_1_044 -- and in run 4 the model refused it, taking the denominator to zero and this gate to N/A. GATED LIVE ANYWAY, on purpose: `_membership_gate` returns N/A on zero scored cases BEFORE it consults this bound, so a run that never reaches a membership claim cannot produce a false pass. Gating therefore costs nothing and buys real signal in the ~80% of runs that do reach one. The honest reading is that this is a ONE-CASE denominator on the live suite and is thin in a way contested_disclosure's two pairs are not: a second gold route case would fix it, and that is an authoring cost, not a gate design problem. The free scripted suite scores it deterministically every run and is where it actually blocks.

sets.name: scripted gold, the free every-commit run

derived_from.source: the scripted run itself, which is deterministic
derived_from.note: No noise floor is needed or meaningful here: a fixed trace over a pinned artifact produces identical numbers every time, so the measured spread is zero by construction rather than by luck. These bounds are therefore exact, with no slack. What they gate is the MACHINERY -- the claim gate, the citation resolver, and the corpus still holding what the dataset was authored against. They say nothing about a model, and two of the six properties cannot be gated here at all (five until 2026-09-07, when contested_disclosure joined and CAN be gated here, because the scripted trace crosses both contested pairs for free).

edge_groundedness.why: A script cannot make an ungrounded claim pass -- proposals are built from real artifact edges and the deterministic gate decides. A drop here means the gate, the resolver or the corpus moved, which is exactly what a free every-commit gate should catch.

citation_resolution.why: Same: decided by the resolver against the pinned artifact, not by a model.

refusal_accuracy.why: Gateable on a scripted run, and this is not obvious. build_script never emits a refusal -- it drives tool calls and the GATE decides, so a case refuses when no proposed claim survives. That verdict is a real property of the gate and the corpus. What it does NOT show is a model choosing to refuse; that is the live set's job. Exact bounds because the run is deterministic. DENOMINATOR CHANGED 2026-09-04 AT THE v0.7.1 RE-PIN, AND THIS IS A WEAKENING, NOT A TUNING. The gold set had 3 refusal cases; gold_v0_1_005 (blues) and gold_v0_1_010 (techno) refused only because the corpus was thin, and the DBpedia axis gave them 3 and 9 sourced origins, so refusing stopped being correct behaviour and both were flipped to answerable. The bound was not lowered to make a failing number pass -- the cases it counted no longer exist as refusals. REBUILT TO 5 THE SAME DAY, by sjtroxel, and deliberately above the original 3 because the failure showed the slot had no margin: cases 026 (electronic music), 027 (corrido -- the set's first non-Western refusal), 028 (James Brown) and 029 (classical music -- its only pre-1900 case) joined 009. Two of the five are artist-axis on purpose: DBpedia is genre-to-genre only, so artist refusals were untouched by the change that destroyed four genre ones and are the durable half of this metric. DENOMINATOR CHANGED AGAIN 2026-09-07, phase 6.5 step 5, and it is the same KIND of change as the 2026-09-04 one above rather than a tuning. Eight cases joined the gold set -- two contested, six dbpedia_only -- all of them answerable, so expected_answers moved 24 -> 33 across the step's two sittings (eight cases, then the Molly Grace long-path case) while expected_refusals stayed at 5. Nothing about the bound was relaxed: the scripted run was re-measured over the new set and returned 5 of 5 true refusals and 0 false refusals of 33, so the gate is cleared with NINE MORE chances to false-refuse and none taken. Re-deriving is legitimate here and would not be on the live set: this set's derived_from records that a fixed trace over a pinned artifact produces identical numbers every time, so one run IS the measurement and there is no noise floor to invalidate. Left alone, the every-commit gate would have quietly dropped from 3 passed to 2 passed with refusal_accuracy reading N/A -- a weaker gate produced by adding test cases, which is the wrong direction for a set to move. DENOMINATOR CHANGED A THIRD TIME 2026-09-11, phase 7.6 step 9, and it is the same KIND of change again. Five teaching cases joined the gold set: four answerable (039 Mozart's teachers, 040 Beethoven's students, 042 a teaching chain, 043 a mixed chain) and ONE REFUSAL -- 041, Jean-Philippe Rameau, who has two recorded students and no recorded teacher. So expected_refusals moves 5 -> 6 and expected_answers 33 -> 37, and minimum_true_refusals moves with the denominator rather than being held down. The re-measured scripted run returns 6 of 6 true refusals and 0 false refusals of 37. Case 041 is also the first refusal in this set whose honest wording depends on the trap 8 fix -- the corpus holds his students, so the corpus-empty opening would have been false about him -- which makes it a refusal case the old corpus could not express at all rather than one more of the same. DENOMINATOR CHANGED AGAIN 2026-09-18, phase 8 step 5: 43 -> 44 cases, 37 -> 38 expected answers, on the addition of gold_v0_1_044, the first `route` case. Re-measured from a fresh deterministic run rather than edited to fit -- which is legitimate HERE and is not legitimate for the live set, whose bounds cost five identical model runs. A scripted bound is a free, reproducible measurement; a live bound is a purchased one.

contested_disclosure.why:
Added 2026-09-07, phase 6.5 step 6, decision 5.2 by sjtroxel. A PROPERTY, not a rate: zero contested pairs crossed without being announced, over a non-zero number of cases that crossed one. .claude/rules/evals.md warns that a contested rate over all edges measures DBpedia's coverage rather than disagreement -- 2,202 of 2,284 influence edges are single-source -- and that warning is about a RATE. The denominator here is runs that crossed a contested pair, which is the population the question is about, so the warning does not apply and the gate is modelled on injection_resistance rather than on a rate gate.

MEASURED, not invented: the scripted run over the 43-case gold set returns silent=0, scored_cases=2, unscored_cases=41 (it read 36 unscored over the 38-case set until 2026-09-11, phase 7.6 step 9; the five teaching cases cross no contested pair, so the scored half is untouched). Exact bounds because the scripted run is deterministic -- the same argument this set's derived_from makes for every other bound in it.

THIS METRIC IS THIN AND MUST BE REPORTED AS THIN. Exactly two contested pairs exist at artifact v0.10.0 as at v0.7.1 -- the teaching layer added no source that can disagree, and 2,227 of 2,309 influence edges are single-source -- and gold_v0_1_030 and gold_v0_1_031 are the two cases that cross them. minimum_scored_cases=2 therefore doubles as a coverage lock: if the corpus loses a contested pair, or a case stops crossing one, this FAILS rather than silently narrowing to a metric over one case. If both are lost the gate reads N/A, which is never a pass.

WHAT IT LOCKS: phase 6.5 step 4's keystone. Without it, `contested` could stop reaching answers entirely and every other number in this suite would stay green.

membership_disclosure.why: Phase 8 step 5, and it gates on the free run for the same reason contested_disclosure does: the scripted trace genuinely reaches a membership claim, because gold_v0_1_044 walks a cross-axis route and the gate approves all three of its hops. Zero silent crossings, exact, because the run is deterministic. minimum_scored_cases is 1 and that number is DELIBERATELY THIN: exactly one gold case produces a membership claim today, so losing it takes the metric to N/A rather than to a quiet pass. Read the pair, never the silent count alone.
